A [[power forward]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]] and was selected by Boston with the 27th overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]]. ==Early life and high school career== Cenac grew up in [[New Orleans]]. He attended [[Riverside Academy (Louisiana)|Riverside Academy]] as a freshman before transferring to [[Isidore Newman School]], where he sat out his sophomore season under transfer rules. As a junior, he helped Newman win its third consecutive state championship and averaged 13.9 points, 10.2 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.9 steals, and 1.3 blocks per game.{{Cite magazine |last=Ebanks |first=Jared |title=Chris Cenac Jr Has a New Home at Link Academy and His Sights Set on a National Championship |url=https://slamonline.com/the-magazine/253/chris-cenac-jr/ |magazine=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |date=December 27, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} After his junior year, he transferred to [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]] in [[Branson, Missouri]]. During the summer of 2024, Cenac was named the most valuable player of the NBPA Top 100 Camp. In March 2025, he helped Link Academy win the inaugural [[Nike EYBL Scholastic]] conference tournament and was named tournament MVP.{{Cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=Link Academy Takes Inaugural Nike EYBL Scholastic Conference Tournament Crown |url=https://nikeeyblscholastic.com/news/2025/3/8/mens-basketball-link-academy-takes-inaugural-nike-eybl-scholastic-conference-tournament-crown.aspx |website=Nike EYBL Scholastic |date=March 8, 2025 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Cenac was a consensus five-star recruit and was ranked among the top ten players in the 2025 class by major recruiting services.{{Cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |author-link2=Paul Biancardi |title=Houston lands C Chris Cenac Jr., its highest-ranked recruit in modern era |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/42629094/houston-lands-c-chris-cenac-jr-highest-ranked-recruit-modern-era |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 26, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} On November 26, 2024, he committed to Houston, choosing the Cougars over a final group that also included [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], and [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Tennessee]]. He was selected for the 2025 [[McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]], and [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. ==College career== Cenac played one season for Houston in 2025–26. He started 36 of 37 games and averaged 9.5 points, a team-leading 7.9 rebounds, 0.7 assists, 0.8 steals, and 0.5 blocks per game.{{Cite web |title=2025–26 Men's Basketball Cumulative Statistics |url=https://uhcougars.com/sports/mens-basketball/stats/2025-26 |website=University of Houston Athletics |access-date=July 11, 2026}} He was named to the NABC All-Gulf District second team as Houston finished 30–7 and reached the Sweet Sixteen of the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]].{{Cite web |title=NABC Announces Division I All-District Teams, Coaches of the Year |url=https://nabc.com/nabc_releases/2026/nabc-announces-division-i-all-district-teams-coaches-of-the-year-2/ |website=National Association of Basketball Coaches |date=March 17, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} On April 9, 2026, Cenac declared for the 2026 NBA draft. The following day, he said that he had hired an agent and was fully committed to remaining in the draft.{{Cite news |last=Duarte |first=Joseph |title=UH's Chris Cenac Jr. explains decision to enter NBA draft. 'One-and-done was always the goal' |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/college/cougars/article/chris-cenac-nba-draft-uh-22200418.php |work=[[Houston Chronicle]] |date=April 10, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} ==Professional career== On June 23, 2026, Cenac was selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 27th overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |last=Snow |first=Taylor |title=No. 27 Pick Chris Cenac Jr. Brings Size, Athleticism and Motor to Boston |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar-nbadraft-260623-no-27-pick-chris-cenac-jr-brings-size-athleticism-and-upside-to-boston |website=Boston Celtics |date=June 23, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} He signed his rookie contract with Boston on July 6.{{Cite news |last=Thompson |first=Khari A. |title=Celtics sign first-round pick Chris Cenac Jr. |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2026/07/06/celtics-sign-first-round-pick-chris-cenac-jr/ |work=Boston.com |date=July 6, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Cenac was also named to the Celtics' roster for the [[2026 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Celtics Announce 2026 NBA Summer League Roster and Schedule |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press-release-20260708-celtics-announce-2026-nba-summer-league-roster-and-schedule |website=Boston Celtics |date=July 8, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} ==National team career== Cenac represented the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States under-17 team]] at the [[2024 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]]. He averaged 8.9 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 1.1 assists in seven games as the United States won the gold medal.{{Cite web |title=Chris Cenac – FIBA U17 Basketball World Cup 2024 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/249-fiba-u17-basketball-world-cup/208542/players/369233-chris-cenac |website=[[FIBA]] |access-date=July 11, 2026}}{{Cite web |title=Chris Cenac Jr. |url=https://www.usab.com/players/chris-cenac-jr |website=USA Basketball |access-date=July 11, 2026}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2025–26]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] | 37 || 36 || 24.8 || .485 || .333 || .621 || 7.9 || .7 || .8 || .5 || 9.5 {{S-end}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * [https://uhcougars.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/chris-cenac-jr-/9544 Houston Cougars bio] * [https://www.usab.com/players/chris-cenac-jr USA Basketball profile] {{Boston Celtics current roster}} {{2026 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Cenac, Chris}} [[Category:2007 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from New Orleans]] [[Category:Boston Celtics draft picks]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Houston Cougars men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Power forwards]]
